2. Facts, in brief, are that the respondent Nos. 1-7 instituted Title Suit No. 57 of 1994 in the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Dhaka for declarations that the order dated 23-10-1976 of the Addition Deputy Commissioner (Rev), the defendant No.2, for forfeiture the suit land is illegal and has no binding force in law and their right title and interest in the suit land have not been affected thereby and that they entitled to get decree for khas possession of the suit land on the averments that the suit land originally belonged to Abdul Ali a purchaser from the CS recorded owner, and Rustom Ali, the Predecessor in interest of the plaintiffs, by registered sale deed dated 16-9-1958 purchased the suit land from Abdul Ali and Rustam Ali was inducted into possession thereof; then Rustom Ali and his wife Sarifunnessa submitted a plan to DIT for construction of a building on the suit land and vide Memo dated 23-11-70, the Authorized Officer of DIT in the early part of the year 1970 approved the same; the dwelling tin-sheds of Rustam Ali were blown away by a devastating storm which resulted in shifting of the of the residence of Rustom Ali to 45/5, Bamacharan Chakarborty Road, old Dhaka; taking the advantage of the absence of Rustom Ali from the suit land, some unknown person at first began to use the 100 feet wide DIT Road adjacent to the suit land for selling therein local vegetables and daily necessaries under open sky and with the passage of time they began to sit on the suit land which was then lying vacant and then the defendant petitioner Nos. 1-7 conspired to set up market on the suit land and with that end in view they approached the authority concerned for allowing them to use the land of plot No.260 including the suit land by converting the same into a market and accordingly the Minister concerned asked the ADC (Rev) Dhaka, the defendant respondent No.8, to deal with the matter; then when Rustom Ali, on collecting materials, went up for construction on the suit land, the defendant petitioner Nos. 1-7 illegally resisted him from setting up a market on the suit land; thereafter, Rustom Ali submitted an application on 30-1-1994 to the Ministry of LA and LR informing the alleged incident and praying for his possession in the suit land then the defendant petitioner Nos. 4-6 filed also an application to the same Ministry praying for allowing them for set up a market on the suit land; then the Ministry of LA and LR asked the ADC (Rev) Dhaka to look into the matter whereupon a local inquiry was conducted by a Kananga who eventually submitted his report with the finding that land in question belongs to Rustom Ali and so for establishment of the proposed Market, the suit land is to be acquired and in that case a huge amount of compensations will be required to be paid to Rustom Ali; thus having failed to established a market on the suit land in a regular way, the defendant petitioners managed to create a so called notice and under Ordinance No. XIX of 1956 and Act No. 12 of 67 and procured the impugned order of forfeiture, which is manifestly illegal. The defendant petitioner Nos. 1-3, 6 and 8 contested the suit and filed three sets of written statements and their common case is that the suit is barred by the provision of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, principle of limitation and estoppels. The defendant petitioner Nos. 1-3 in their written statement contended that the plaintiffs established market on the suit land without prior permission from the Collector as required under the provisions of Ordinance No.XIX of 1959 and Act No. XII of 1967 and the notice of forfeiture was duly served upon Rustom Ali, but he did not turn up before the authority in time and accordingly vide the order dated 23-10-1976 passed in Miscellaneous Case No.2 of 1976 as per provisions of Hat and Bazars Ordinance, 1959, the suit land including the Bazar was forfeited by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, and that the Bazar including the suit land is locally known as Rampura Bazar which has been established a full-fledged Bazar as defined under section 2(12) and section 20(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and after forfeiture, the government took possession of the above Bazar and handed over the management of the said Bazar to Dhaka Municipal Corporation and that the Bazar was taken over by the government on 23-10-76 but this suit was filed in 1986, after lapse of 10 years, as such the sit barred by limitation. The defendant petitioner No.6, the Secretary, Rampura Bazar Kallyan Samity, filed written statement con- tending that Rustam Ali, established Bazar in the suit land without obtained permission of the Collector as required under Ordinance No.XIX of 1995 and before passing the order of forfeiture, a notice to show cause was duly served upon Rustom Ali but he did not give the reply to the same with in time and consequently government lawfully forfeited the said Bazar together with the suit land on 23-10-76 and subsequently the government left the management of the said Bazar with Dhaka Municipal Corporation which granted allotment to as many as 83 shop-owners who have been running business therein since 1972 and the suit is barred by limitation. The defendant petitioner No.8, Dhaka City Corporation, filed written statement contending that Rustom Ali set up a private market on the suit land without having prior permission from the government and the local people used to sell and purchase daily commodities in the said market and when the matter came to the notice of the government, Rustom Ali was asked to show cause as to why the said private market set up by him would not be forfeited and he then filed a representation but the same being found unsatisfactory, the government vide order dated 23-10-76 forfeited said market including suit land and thereafter government handed over the management, control and physical possession of the said market to Dhaka Municipal Corporation on 15-1-79 and the said market is being managed and controlled by Dhaka Municipal Corporation and the plaintiffs were fully divested of all their right, title and interest on the suit land since 23-10-76. The learned Subordinate Judge, after hearing decreed the suit. The defendant petitioners then filed three sets of appeals being First Appeal No. 70 of 1995, First Appeal No.88 of 1995 and First Appeal No.274 of 1994 and the High Court Division, after hearing those analogously, dismissed the appeals. 

 3. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the plaintiff respondents having established a market on the suit land without prior permission from the Collector as required under the provisions of Ordinance No.XIX of 1959 and Act XII of 1967, the suit land including the bazaar was duly forfeited by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka vide order dated 23-10-76 passed in Misc. Case No. VIII-2/76 as per provision of Hats and Bazar Ordinance 1969 and that before forfeiture, due notice was served upon Rustom Ali but he failed to turn up and so the land was duly forfeited and after forfeiture, the government has taken possession over of the Bazar and the said Bazar, which is locally known as Rampura Bazar, having been established as a full-fledged Bazar as defined under section 20(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the government has handed over the management of the said Bazar to Dhaka Municipal Corporation and the said Bazar having being taken over by the government on 23-10-79 and the present suit having been filed in 1984, after a lapse of 8 years is barred by limitation and further in his Report (Exhibit B) the Kanoongo stated that Rustom Ali having established a private market on the suit land have been collecting tolls therefrom but the learned Subordinate Judge did not consider the same and without any basis held that Exhibits A and B as fraudulent pieces of documents.
